title: Georges Bizet's birth chart
metaDescription: Georges Bizet's chart, computed from a sourced birth date: Sun at 1.6° Scorpio. Birth time unknown, so no houses or rising sign.
lede: The chart's headline is a sextile: Mercury and Mars within 0.7°, thinking wired to drive. A sextile pays out only on effort; the scheme calls it opportunity rather than gift.

blocks.title: Where the Sun actually stood
blocks.text: The Sun sits at 1.6° Scorpio — the first decan, 0°–10°, which the tradition sub-rules by Mars. Degrees matter more than the sign label here: two people born a fortnight apart share Scorpio and share almost nothing else about where the Sun actually stood.

blocks.title: The fast planets
blocks.text: Closer in, Mercury stands at 25.1° Libra; Venus stands at 18.3° Libra; Mars stands at 24.4° Leo. The tradition reads a mind at home in argument and pattern from Mercury, taste led by wit and proportion from Venus, drive that ignites on contact from Mars.

blocks.title: The angles that hold
blocks.text: The tightest geometry in the chart puts Mercury a sixth of the circle apart from Mars, 0.7° off exact. A sextile pays out only on effort; the scheme calls it opportunity rather than gift. Behind it, Jupiter trine Neptune at 1.5°, and Venus opposition Pluto at 1.7° — both still well inside the orbs this site uses. Each angle here was measured at every hour of the civil day and held; whatever the missing clock said, this geometry was in it.

blocks.title: What the angles build
blocks.text: The Moon stands apart from every major angle the day held — the tradition reads an unaspected planet as a voice that speaks on its own schedule, unmodulated by the rest of the chart.

blocks.title: The classical map
blocks.text: Two planets here sit in a sign the classical scheme scores. The Moon in Capricorn at 20.7° is in detriment — the planet opposite its home, working against the grain; Venus in Libra at 18.3° is in domicile — the planet in its own sign, running on home rules. Condition, not character: that is all the dignity table ever measured.

blocks.title: The shape of the whole
blocks.text: Balance, counted honestly across the 10 placements whose signs hold for the whole day: elements air 4, water 3, fire 2, earth 1; modalities cardinal 5, fixed 4, mutable 1. Uranus and Pluto were retrograde — the backward drift a body appears to make as the Earth overtakes it, read in the scheme as a function that reviews before it releases.

blocks.title: The Moon, and how far it can move
blocks.text: The Moon stayed in Capricorn for the whole of that day at the birthplace, covering 13.3° between midnight and midnight. That is quick enough to make the exact degree a neighbourhood rather than an address, and slow enough to leave the sign settled. At the noon reference it stands at 20.7°.
